name: Biff Bang Pow!
label: Creation Records
lede: Alan McGee's label gave the world the Jesus and Mary Chain, My Bloody Valentine and Oasis. It also gave his own band half a dozen albums, most of them cut in a few days, with two of the label's co-founders in the line-up.

eras.title: A label and a band out of the same pocket
eras.text: Alan McGee had played in The Laughing Apple and run a club night, the Living Room, in central London. In 1983 he quit British Rail, started Creation Records with Dick Green and Joe Foster on a £1,000 bank loan, and gave himself a band too. Both took their names from The Creation, his favourite 1960s group.

years.cap: Biff Bang Pow! live at the M.J.C. Claudel, Reims
years.src: Wikipedia: Biff Bang Pow! · Wikipedia: Alan McGee · Wikipedia: Creation Records
years.h: McGee names his band after a song by the Creation
years.p: Alan McGee on guitar and vocals, Dick Green on guitar, Joe Foster on bass and Ken Popple on drums. Three of the four also run the new Creation Records.
years.xp: The name comes from 'Biff Bang Pow', a song by the 1960s mod band [[The Creation|1d5d9b06-1b0b-4c40-8481-bad62e03b4ab]], the same band the label is named for. McGee had already been through H2O and the Laughing Apple with his Glasgow friend [[Andrew Innes|213b0443-e41c-40d7-b8c2-0bcb4f2b6e57]].

years.h: 'Fifty Years of Fun' is Creation single CRE 003
years.p: Each copy came in a hand-painted, spray-painted fold-out sleeve in a clear bag, with the run-out grooves etched by hand. The B-side is 'Then When I Scream'.

years.src: Vivonzeureux: J.C. Brouchard · Louder Than War
years.h: Creation's first French show, at a youth centre in Reims
years.p: The [[Jasmine Minks|c3552faf-9c1c-46ba-af13-653fe2fdcf9c]] headline the MJC Claudel, with Biff Bang Pow! and [[The Jesus and Mary Chain|e938a15c-b17e-4e7a-9f68-ff0d536cab44]] in support. A local fan, J.C. Brouchard, puts it on.
years.xp: Brouchard says McGee "created" him that year, and he went on to run the band's fan club and write sleeve notes. The European tour with the Minks and the Mary Chain that followed was, in the band's word, "bonkers".

years.src: Wikipedia: Alan McGee · Discogs: Biff Bang Pow!
years.h: The Jesus and Mary Chain's 'Upside Down' changes the label
years.p: McGee is now managing [[The Jesus and Mary Chain|e938a15c-b17e-4e7a-9f68-ff0d536cab44]], and their first single comes out on Creation. Biff Bang Pow! follows the same year with 'There Must Be a Better Life'.

eras.title: Paintbrushes, beat hotels and a man in Reims
eras.text: The first albums pulled mod, psychedelia and new wave together, and a 1986 single got the band into the indie top ten. Running jokes and dedications to a Frenchman named J.C. Brouchard ran through the sleeves.

years.src: Discogs: Pass the Paintbrush · Louder Than War · Wikipedia: Biff Bang Pow!
years.h: Pass the Paintbrush, Honey.. is Creation LP number 4
years.p: Eight songs cut at Alaska Studios, with Joe Foster at the controls, from 'There Must Be a Better Life' to 'A Day Out with Jeremy Chester'. The sleeve dedicates it to "our dear friend, J.C. Brouchard," of Reims.
play: There Must Be a Better Life

years.cap: Biff Bang Pow!, Creation Records press photo, c. 1986
years.src: Wikipedia: Biff Bang Pow! · Vivonzeureux: Someone Stole My Wheels · Section 26 · Louder Than War
years.h: 'Love's Going Out of Fashion' reaches No. 6 on the indie chart
years.p: The band's highest placing on the UK Independent Chart. 'Someone Stole My Wheels' follows in October, credited to "J.C. Brouchard with Biff Bang Pow!"
years.xp:
The Frenchman doesn't play on it. Brouchard says his whole contribution was posing for Luke Hayes's camera by the Thames on the Isle of Dogs for the label photos. The song had once been lined up as a Revolving Paint Dream single, 'Wheels on My Scooter'.

On October 25 the band played Reims again, and the show was filmed for the video, without proper lights. McGee still counts 'Love's Going Out of Fashion' and 'Someone Stole My Wheels' among the band's good ones.

years.cap: Poster for Biff Bang Pow! at the M.J.C. Claudel, Reims
years.src: Discogs: The Girl Who Runs the Beat Hotel · Louder Than War · Wikipedia: Biff Bang Pow!
years.h: The Girl Who Runs the Beat Hotel ends on Brouchard again
years.p: Both 1986 singles open it, and the last track is 'The Whole World Is Turning Brouchard!'. The sleeve credits J.C. Brouchard's "spiritual guidance" and prints his street address in Reims.
years.xp: It made a Top 50 indie albums of the year list, which the band still mention.
play: The Girl Who Runs the Beat Hotel

years.cap: Flyer for Biff Bang Pow!, House of Love and Holler at the Richmond, March 19, 1987
years.src: Discogs: Oblivion · Louder Than War · Wikipedia: Biff Bang Pow! · Discogs: A Better Life
years.h: Oblivion comes out as a mid-price LP "for the kids"
years.p: [[Dave Evans|3d441f4a-4de7-48fc-bb2f-6d98678af5a7]] plays bass and Andrew Innes adds organ and guitar part-time. The sticker: "Doing It For The Kids," for a limited period only.
years.xp:
Evans says they had a week booked at Alaska Studios: tracks on Monday and Tuesday, then [[Primal Scream|55704c38-224f-4b75-b29f-d43653f8bc9a]] took the Wednesday slot, and the band mixed on Thursday and Friday. McGee says Oblivion sold about 10,000 copies in the States.

Innes had played with [[Bobby Gillespie|23bb4a17-70b1-4ae8-9f46-fbbfcb868b24]] in the Drains back in 1978. Dick Green calls him the one "truly truly great musician" in the band. Evans joined the Mary Chain for a short spell later in 1987. A live set from Dortmund that February stayed in the vaults until the 2022 box set.

eras.title: Acid house, sad eyes and Me
eras.text: As Creation moved toward My Bloody Valentine and the dance floor, McGee's band kept making guitar pop, each record sadder than the last and each one made in days. Edward Ball of Television Personalities became a fixture.

years.h: McGee walks off the French tour halfway through
years.p: Brouchard, left to deal with it, says McGee quit "in the most rock'n'roll fashion." It's the end of his time as the band's "spiritual advisor".

years.h: Love Is Forever, cut at Greenhouse Studios in December 1987
years.p: [[Philip King|bee38d85-fe86-4ff7-b430-7d63edf9d3e6]], later of [[Lush|697801d1-68b2-4413-a7e4-0ef507d21cc1]] and the Mary Chain, plays bass; Edward Ball sings backing vocals. It opens with 'Miss California Toothpaste 1972'.

years.h: The Acid House Album has no acid house on it
years.p: Released at the height of the dance craze, it's a 14-song Biff Bang Pow! compilation of singles, alternate takes and demos, each sleeve hand-sprayed and stickered.

years.src: Discogs: Songs for the Sad Eyed Girl · Louder Than War
years.h: Three days in Fulham and Walthamstow make Songs for the Sad Eyed Girl
years.p: Seven songs recorded in autumn 1989, Ball on organ and piano, Green producing with Ian Shaw. 'The Girl from Well Lane' was taped live that May.
years.xp: It's McGee's favourite of the albums: "I think that album sold about 10,000 copies which isn't bad." His verdict on the band overall is gentler on the songs than the players: "the group slightly let down the songs."
play: Songs for the Sad Eyed Girl

years.src: Discogs: Me · Wikipedia: Biff Bang Pow!
years.h: Me, made in six days, is the last Biff Bang Pow! album
years.p: Recorded in December 1990 at Jam in Finsbury Park and Granny's in Fulham, with [[Robert Young|447d9deb-9c22-4f71-ab87-fdcaa820fea6]] of Primal Scream on guitar and [[Paul Mulreany|6a21ac54-b38e-4c89-be1c-ebf15fb7d19d]] on vocals.

years.src: Wikipedia: Biff Bang Pow! · Discogs: Biff Bang Pow!
years.p: Creation's 1984–1991 compilation is the band's last record. Debasement Tapes, a second collection, follows in 1992.

eras.title: Foster's mixtape, then the whole box
eras.text: Creation closed at the end of 1999. The songs came back twice: once picked by Joe Foster, once all of them.

years.p: The founding bassist, by now running the reissue label Rev-Ola, picks the collection himself.

years.src: Discogs: A Better Life · Louder Than War · Wilfully Obscure · Wikipedia: Biff Bang Pow!
yt: A Better Life box set trailer
years.h: Cherry Red's six-CD A Better Life collects everything
years.p: A Better Life: Complete Creations 1984–1991 adds the Dortmund concert, unreleased songs, and demos by the Laughing Apple and McGee with [[Jowe Head|3863fd93-5820-4574-9585-f30d71cfbaa5]].
